static.vertical: Infrastructure field services (utility, municipal, and industrial inspection/construction-support/repair/maintenance)
static._archetype_note: JUDGMENT CALL: 'consumer-inventory' clearly does not fit (no consumer/D2C sales). The closer call is 'asset-heavy-industrial' vs 'services-project'. Chose asset-heavy-industrial because the collateral and balance sheet are genuinely EQUIPMENT-led, not just receivables-led: Net Property and Equipment ($53.1M) is ~39% of Total Assets ($134.5M) at June 2026 -- larger than Accounts Receivable ($18.1M) or Inventory ($9.8M) -- and the security agreement pledges 'machinery, vehicles, and equipment' as a named collateral category alongside accounts and inventory (equipment yards in Albany, Syracuse, and Buffalo per the Information Certificate). The IC memo and management presentation also frame the business around 'backlog visibility' and 'crew utilization/materials purchasing/change-order capture' driving margin -- close to asset-heavy-industrial's 'backlog and book-to-bill, margin vs volume (absorption)' KPI emphasis. 'services-project' was the other real candidate (payroll-heavy field crews, project/milestone billing, unbilled-AR dynamics) and would also be defensible; flagging both for the analyst since the memo does not itself use either label and this is a genuinely close call between a construction/field-services contractor (asset-heavy-industrial-ish but not a manufacturer) and a project-services business (services-project-ish but with real owned equipment as collateral, not just cash-flow-based recovery).

facility.instrument: Senior secured term loan, single tranche, fully funded at closing
facility.draw_structure: Single advance at closing (2025-01-15); no delayed-draw or revolving capacity. Proceeds refinanced legacy debt in full -- no proceeds retained for later borrowing.
facility.interest_rate: SOFR + 6.25% cash interest, subject to a 2.00% SOFR floor (effective minimum all-in rate 8.25%); interest payable monthly in arrears; overdue amounts bear an additional 2.00% default margin. No PIK. Scheduled monthly principal amortization of 0.60% of beginning funded debt, due with monthly interest.
facility.oid: None disclosed. $3,000,000.00 of closing fees were capitalized as a 'Deferred Financing Fees' balance-sheet asset and are amortized straight-line at exactly $50,000.00/month (verified constant across every month checked, 2025-01 through 2026-06; $3,000,000 / 60 months = $50,000/month, matching the facility's 5-year term) -- funded entirely by the $12,000,000 sponsor equity contribution at closing rather than financed into the loan balance, consistent with the Fee Letter's own statement that fees 'do not increase funded debt.'

our_view.thesis_status: All four thesis pillars remain intact through the full 6-quarter history reviewed (2025 Q1 through 2026 Q2). Total Leverage Ratio has improved every single quarter since close -- 3.3304x (2025 Q1) -> 2.8972x -> 2.6612x -> 2.5098x -> 2.4235x -> 2.3911x (2026 Q2) -- comfortably inside the 5.50x maximum with a wide and widening cushion (~57% headroom at June 2026), driven by contractual amortization and steady EBITDA growth (TTM Covenant EBITDA $24.5M vs FY2024 UW EBITDA $17.5M). Cash has built every quarter ($27.3M -> $36.4M). Revenue and EBITDA beat the approved budget in 5 of the last 6 quarters; June 2026 is the FIRST quarter with a negative variance (-$59,787.70 revenue, -$85,898.18 EBITDA vs the monthly plan), but both misses are small (<0.5% and <3.7% respectively) and both revenue ($13.16M) and EBITDA ($2.29M) are still up year-over-year (+6.2% and +9.3% vs June 2025). No customer, collections, or covenant stress is evident: AR aging buckets have grown roughly in proportion to revenue with no material bucket-mix deterioration across the months sampled, and no restatement, correction notice, or lender query appears anywhere in the Portfolio Management or Period Archive history (unlike Nemeris's corrected Q2 2026 covenant calc or Asteron's restructuring). This reads as a clean, steadily deleveraging credit; watchlist is off.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: A second consecutive quarter of negative budget variance on revenue or EBITDA, a Total Leverage Ratio reversal (an increase quarter-over-quarter rather than the steady decline seen to date), a material AR aging bucket shift toward 61-90/90+ (collections/retainage risk crystallizing), or loss of a top-5 customer/project would move trajectory toward 'stable' or 'deteriorating' and warrant turning the watchlist on.

Flagged for the analyst's own read at the next review -- this is a genuinely clean credit on the evidence reviewed, with no restructuring, no correction history, and comfortable covenant headroom, but the June 2026 first-ever negative budget variance is worth a second look next cycle before the analyst signs off on 'improving' continuing.
